name: Transfer pricing and intra-group profit shifting abuse
description: Related companies set prices, fees, royalties or interest on goods, services, intellectual property and loans between themselves in ways that move taxable profit to low-tax or secrecy jurisdictions. Abuse is typically visible as charges that exceed arm's-length norms, services with no deliverable, or recipient entities that lack the people or assets to justify the income. Banks, trade-finance providers and corporate service providers see the payments, invoices and structures even if they do not see the tax returns.

sources.text: OECD, Transfer Pricing Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises and Tax Administrations, 2022
OECD, BEPS Actions 8-10: Aligning Transfer Pricing Outcomes with Value Creation, 2015
OECD, Illicit Financial Flows from Developing Countries: Measuring OECD Responses, 2014

indicators.name: Transaction price materially different from market value
indicators.canon: Transaction price materially different from market value
indicators.desc: Price paid differs sharply from market value, comparable sales or estimates without commercial justification.
indicators.ctx: Goods sold or bought between group companies at prices well above or below independent benchmarks.
indicators.fp: Distressed sales, rare items, quality differences or volatile markets.

indicators.name: Fee arrangements disproportionate to services or paid by third parties
indicators.canon: Fee arrangements disproportionate to services or paid by third parties
indicators.ctx: Management, consulting or service fees paid to an affiliate are out of proportion to the services or to the payer's size.

indicators.name: Vague invoices for unspecified services
indicators.desc: Invoices describe 'consulting', 'marketing support' or 'liaison services' without deliverables, timesheets or reports.
indicators.ctx: Intra-group invoices describe services only in general terms, with no deliverables, hours or output.
indicators.fp: Early-stage or informal advisers may keep thin paperwork.

indicators.name: Loan with no commercial purpose or unusual terms
indicators.canon: Loan with no commercial purpose or unusual terms
indicators.desc: Interest-free, no repayments, or terms inconsistent with market.
indicators.ctx: Intercompany loans have no commercial purpose, unusually high interest, or no repayment pattern, shifting profit by interest.

indicators.name: Complex layered structure without commercial rationale
indicators.canon: Complex layered structure without commercial rationale
indicators.desc: Multiple tiers of entities, trusts or foundations, often across secrecy or low-transparency jurisdictions, with no evident business or tax reason.
indicators.ctx: Group structure inserts intermediate entities in several jurisdictions between operating companies and the ultimate parent with no operational reason.
indicators.fp: Legitimate groups, estate planning and fund structures can be complex; request an explanation and structure chart.

indicators.name: No evidence of real operations
indicators.desc: Business shows little or no staff, premises, web presence or client base consistent with its stated activities and turnover.
indicators.ctx: Affiliate receiving the fees or royalties has no staff, premises or evidence of performing the functions it charges for.
indicators.fp: Small consultancies or home-based businesses may have a light footprint; request supporting contracts and invoices.

indicators.name: Secrecy or low-transparency jurisdiction nexus
indicators.desc: Entities, accounts or assets are booked in jurisdictions offering strong secrecy or limited transparency, including where unrelated to the entity's operations.
indicators.ctx: Recurring payments flow from operating companies to affiliates in low-tax or secrecy jurisdictions with no operations.
indicators.fp: Legitimate holding structures and funds use such jurisdictions for tax neutrality or legal reasons.

indicators.name: Payments in and out the same day with thin margin
indicators.canon: Payments in and out the same day with thin margin
indicators.desc: Funds received from buyer are paid onward to supplier, often same day, leaving little retained.
indicators.ctx: A group trading or principal entity receives and re-pays amounts the same day with a thin margin, acting as a conduit for profit.
indicators.fp: Distributors and agents may operate on thin margins and pass-through.

indicators.name: Royalty, licence or intangible-asset payments concentrated in a low-tax affiliate with minimal functions
indicators.canon: Royalty, licence or intangible-asset payments concentrated in a low-tax affiliate with minimal functions
indicators.desc: Recurring payments for brands, software or intellectual property go to a related entity in a low-tax jurisdiction that has little staff, development activity or control over the asset.
indicators.ctx: Operating companies pay a percentage of revenue as royalties to a group entity in a low-tax jurisdiction that holds the asset but has no development team.
indicators.fp: Many groups hold intellectual property in a central entity for legitimate commercial reasons, and rates may be supported by a formal transfer-pricing study.

indicators.name: Year-end or retrospective price adjustments between related parties
indicators.canon: Year-end or retrospective price adjustments between related parties
indicators.desc: Large true-up, credit-note or compensating payments between group companies at period end that bring profit into line with a target outcome rather than with underlying activity.
indicators.ctx: Material balancing payments between affiliates shortly before the financial year ends, with no matching change in volumes.
indicators.fp: Legitimate transfer-pricing policies often include year-end adjustments to align results with documented arm's-length ranges.
